newsitem.title: USA: W. House offers help to AMR, pilots union.
newsitem.headline: W. House offers help to AMR, pilots union.

text.p: The White House Friday offered to help settle a dispute between American Airlines and its pilots if the parties would like the assistance.

"We are monitoring the dispute very closely. If the parties believe that our participation could help, we obviously would consider how we could play a more constructive role," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.

Florida Senators Bob Graham and Connie Mack on Friday had asked President Clinton in a letter to help AMR Corp's American Airlines and its pilots reach a settlement to avoid a strike that would cripple Florida's winter tourism business.
"I think both parties would have to see a constructive role for us to play in order for us to be useful," McCurry said.
In a letter to the president, Graham and Mack said a strike beginning February 15 would be "costly" and "painful."

"If a settlement is not reached, a mid-February holiday weekend airline strike would disrupt passengers and the flow of freight across our nation and overseas, particularly in our hemisphere," the letter said. "Nowhere would the harm be more acute than in Florida."

Pilots' leaders have said they want to win a new contract now, even if it involves a strike, rather than risk lengthy arbitration. Earlier this week, a senior union leader forecast a 50 percent possibility of a strike that could last up to 60 days.

The two sides planned to begin five days of "supermediation" on Monday, in a last-gasp effort to reach a new four-year labor contract. Those negotiations will take place in Washington with the help of the National Mediation Board.
